result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A draws a clear diverging bar chart of actual minus plan in dollars around a single 'On plan' line, and puts each value label right at the end of its bar. Northfield is clearly marked '$0 (on plan)' with no bar. B's percent view is reasonable and sorted well, but its values sit in a separate column on the far right instead of next to the bars, Northfield is drawn as a thin gray sliver, and the subtitle gives % rather than $ thousands as the unit. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both are sorted diverging bar charts centered on plan, with a clear two-color split for ahead and behind. B puts each dollar-gap label right next to its bar and marks Northfield explicitly as '$0 (on plan)'. A's labels sit in a separate column away from the bars, and Northfield is drawn as a thin grey sliver, though the 0.0% label explains it. A's percent scale is a fair choice, but B's direct labels and clearer on-plan handling make it easier to read at a glance.
